column1: # Carve-outs for tools/check_verdict_exit_status.py (issue #705).
# Every `done < <(…)` under tools/**/*.sh and cpp/test/*.sh is REJECTED unless
# it is named here with the reason it is safe. A process substitution discards
# its producer's exit status by construction (docs/TESTING_STRATEGY.md §3a,
# issue #694), so "the checker found nothing" and "the checker could not run"
# reach the verdict as the same empty stdout.
# Format — three TAB-separated fields:
#   <repo-relative path>
# `anchor` is any substring of that loop's PRODUCER (the text inside `<( … )`,
# across as many lines as its parentheses span) that is unique to it in that
# file. Anchoring on the producer rather than a line number keeps an entry
# attached to the loop it justifies when the file moves around it — and means a
# rewritten producer has to be re-justified. An entry that matches zero loops is
# STALE and an error; one that matches two is AMBIGUOUS and an error; an empty
# reason is an error.
# A reason must say WHICH §3a shape makes the loop safe. There are only two
# available to this construct:
#   floor — an explicit positive floor below the loop turns "nothing came back"
#           into a failure, so an unrunnable producer cannot reach the ok arm.
#   pure  — the producer is a shell builtin / text transformation over a value
#           already in memory (`printf`, `sed`, `find`, `git ls-files`). There is
#           no separate checker whose "could not run" is being mistaken for
#           "clean" — and every one of these ALSO has a floor below it.
# §3a shape 2 (`out="$(check "$f")"; rc=$?`) is unavailable here by
# construction: `$?` after `done < <(cmd)` is the loop's status, never `cmd`'s.
# A loop that genuinely needs a checker's status must be restructured, not
# carved out.
tools/check_conformance_doc_counts.sh
column3: floor+pure: `list_files` is a `git ls-files`/`find` enumeration of the repo's own docs, and the `checked -lt 1` floor below (`the conformance-count guard scanned zero current-status occurrences`) turns an empty walk into a hard error.

column1: tools/check_conformance_doc_counts.sh
column3: floor+pure: `scan_file` is a `grep`/`awk` scan of one already-read file, and the same `checked -lt 1` floor covers this inner loop — a scan that produced nothing for every file cannot reach the ok arm.

column3: floor+pure: a `find` over a directory this script just verified exists, and the `${#files[@]} -eq 0` floor immediately below dies with "the artifact contains no files — nothing to apply" rather than applying nothing quietly.

column1: tools/ci/check_matrix_paths.sh
column3: floor+pure: `printf | sed` over the `$spec` string already in memory, and the `checked -lt 1` floor below ("the mapping check compared ZERO paths — a check that found nothing to check is not a pass") fails closed.
